findings.observation: Reviewed the TIA Determination Worksheet (documentId: be3343ae-a570-434f-8f82-a7e396bcc27b), specifically the TPW Staff Determination section. The worksheet clearly shows that the checkbox for 'A traffic impact analysis is NOT required' is marked with an X. The determination was made by reviewer Manar Hasan on 3/19/2026. The worksheet states that traffic generated by the proposal does not exceed thresholds established in the LDC.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item CC-22-08 has a condition: 'If TIA required per worksheet (generally >2,000 trips/day)'. The TIA Determination Worksheet explicitly indicates that a TIA is NOT required for this project. Since the condition for applicability is not met (TIA is not required), this checklist item does not apply to this site plan submission.
findings.explanation: TIA not required per TIA Determination Worksheet reviewed by TPW staff on 3/19/2026

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) using the vision tool. Two proposed driveways are shown on Collier Street (the north frontage), both labeled 'TYPE II DRIVEWAY SEE SHEET 30 FOR DETAILS'. Both driveways have width dimensions of 30' shown. However, no spacing dimensions are shown measuring the distance between the two driveways, nor are there dimensions showing the distance from either driveway to the nearest street intersection (Collier Street intersections with S Lamar or other streets).
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires driveway spacing dimensions to be shown on plans. While the driveways themselves are depicted and their widths are dimensioned, the spacing between driveways and from driveways to intersections is not dimensioned. Austin's driveway standards require specific spacing criteria to be met and verified, which necessitates showing these dimensions on the site plan for completeness review. The absence of these spacing dimensions constitutes the deficiency described in CC-22-12.
findings.explanation: Two driveways shown on Collier Street but no spacing dimensions between driveways or from intersections
findings.resolution: Add dimension lines on the site plan showing: (1) the spacing distance between the two proposed driveways on Collier Street, and (2) the spacing distance from each driveway to the nearest street intersection.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 13 (site plan) and Sheet 30 (Type II Driveway standard details) using the vision tool. On Sheet 13, both proposed driveways on Collier Street show width dimensions of 30'. Sheet 30 contains the City of Austin Type II Driveway standard detail (433S-2), which includes Note 1: 'ALL TYPE II DRIVEWAYS SHALL HAVE RADIUS ENDS' and Note 2 stating that 'DRIVEWAY WIDTHS AND RADII DIMENSIONS...ARE HIGHLY VARIABLE, SUBJECT TO SITE SPECIFIC CONDITIONS'. However, no curb return radius dimensions (e.g., R=15') are shown at the driveway corners on Sheet 13. The plan labels indicate 'SEE SHEET 30 FOR DETAILS', but Sheet 30 only provides the standard detail, not the site-specific radii values.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires both driveway widths AND curb return radii to be shown on plans. While driveway widths are properly dimensioned at 30', the curb return radii at the corners where the driveways meet Collier Street are not dimensioned. The completeness check requires these site-specific values to be shown on the plan so that TPW can verify compliance with spacing and geometric design requirements. A reference to the standard detail sheet is insufficient without the actual dimensioned radii on the site plan.
findings.explanation: Driveway widths shown (30') on Sheet 13, but curb return radii not dimensioned at driveway corners
findings.resolution: Add curb return radius dimensions (e.g., R=__') at each corner of the two proposed driveways on Collier Street on the site plan.

findings.observation: Used vision tool to examine Sheet 13 for adjacent driveways within 300 feet. Vision analysis identified some adjacent driveways: one on Frank Reeder Subdivision (north of site on Collier near S. Lamar intersection), one on Frank Reeder Subdivision (on S. Lamar north of Collier intersection), and one on Evergreen Heights property (south of site on S. Lamar). However, the plan focuses primarily on the subject site and immediately adjacent ROW. Neighboring lot lines along Collier Street (Roger Wilson Subdivision - Lots 4, 5, 6, 7 labeled on Sheet 14) are shown but no driveway access points are depicted for these immediately adjacent properties.
findings.reasoning: The requirement is to show adjacent driveways within 300 feet of the site to enable Transportation staff to verify driveway spacing compliance. The plan shows some adjacent driveways but not all. Properties immediately adjacent to the site along Collier Street (within 50-150 feet) have no driveways depicted, even though these properties would reasonably have access points. The 300-foot requirement is intended to show the full context for spacing analysis, and the incomplete depiction of adjacent access points prevents proper review.
findings.explanation: Some adjacent driveways shown, but not all within 300 feet; neighboring properties along Collier lack depicted access points.
findings.resolution: Show all adjacent driveways within 300 feet of the site on the plans, including access points for neighboring properties along Collier Street.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 13 using the vision tool. Collier Street, which forms the north frontage of the site, appears to be an undivided street (no median shown). The two proposed driveways on the site's Collier Street frontage can be compared to existing driveways on the north side of Collier Street. The vision analysis noted that 'the western proposed driveway appears to align roughly with the existing driveway for LOT 6 across the street' and 'the eastern proposed driveway does not appear to align directly with an opposing driveway.' However, no dimension lines are shown on the plan measuring the offset distances between the proposed driveways and the opposing existing driveways.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item has a condition: 'If site fronts undivided street'. Collier Street is an undivided street, so the condition is met and the item applies. Austin's transportation standards require offset dimensions from opposing driveways on undivided streets to verify safe sight distance and turning movement conflicts. While the driveways are shown graphically, the specific offset dimensions required for TPW review are not dimensioned on the plan. This constitutes the deficiency described in CC-22-15.
findings.explanation: Site fronts undivided Collier Street with opposing driveways, but offset dimensions not shown on Sheet 13
findings.resolution: Add dimension lines showing the offset distance from the centerline or edge of each proposed driveway to the centerline or edge of the opposing existing driveways across Collier Street.

findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 16 (Site Notes And Tables), specifically Block 1 which contains the '1700 SOUTH LAMAR - PARKING TABLE'. The table shows a column labeled 'PROPOSED USE-MIX' listing: STUDIO (70 units), 1 BEDROOM (328 units), 2 BEDROOM (55 units), 3 BEDROOM (6 units), RESTAURANT (4,888 SF), RETAIL (GENERAL) (5,046 SF), and LEASING OFFICE (5,661 SF). The 'UNITS / SF' column shows unit counts for residential uses and square footage for commercial uses. The table is comprehensive and cross-references to the building information and project tracking tables also on Sheet 16.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires a parking table showing proposed land uses with square footage. Sheet 16's parking table clearly displays all proposed land uses (residential by unit type and commercial by use) along with their associated units or square footage. This satisfies the completeness requirement for TPW to verify parking calculations against land use metrics. The table format and content align with Austin's standard parking table requirements.
findings.explanation: Parking table on Sheet 16 shows all proposed land uses with units/SF breakdown

findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 16 (Site Notes And Tables), specifically Block 1 containing the parking table. The table shows 'TOTAL PRIVATE PARKING SPACES PROVIDED: 647' in a clearly labeled column. Additionally, there is a separate column for 'COLLIER PUBLIC PARALLEL PARKING: 23'. The table also shows bicycle parking with 'REQUIRED' and 'PROVIDED' columns, showing long-term bicycle parking provided as 16 spaces. The 647 total includes the breakdown by type: 500 standard, 57 compact, 31 EV ready, 10 EV capable, and 26 ADA spaces.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires the total number of provided parking spaces (vehicle and bicycle) to be shown. Sheet 16's parking table clearly displays the total private vehicle parking (647 spaces) and bicycle parking (16 long-term spaces provided, with requirements shown as ranges). The table provides complete visibility of all parking provisions, satisfying the completeness requirement for TPW review.
findings.explanation: Sheet 16 parking table shows total parking: 647 vehicle spaces and bicycle parking totals

findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 37 (Building Plan - Level 1) which contains the parking garage layout and a 'SYMBOL LEGEND' in Block 2. The legend provides explicit dimensions for all parking space types: R - REGULAR PARKING SPACE (9'-0" X 17'-0"), C - COMPACT PARKING SPACE (7'-6" X 16'-0"), HC - ACCESSIBLE PARKING SPACE (8'-0" X 18'-0" W/ 5'-0" AISLE), and VAN - VAN ACCESSIBLE PARKING SPACE (16'-0" X 18'-0" W/ 5'-0" AISLE). The legend includes a graphical diagram showing width and depth dimensions. These dimensions are consistent across all building level sheets (37-41) that show parking.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires parking stall width, depth, or angle to be dimensioned. Sheet 37's symbol legend provides comprehensive dimensions for all parking space types, showing both width and depth (and implicitly angle through the floor plan layout). The dimensions are clearly labeled and tied to the parking space symbols used throughout the garage plans. This satisfies the completeness requirement for TPW to verify parking space geometry compliance.
findings.explanation: Sheet 37 symbol legend shows parking stall dimensions for all space types (regular, compact, accessible, van)

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 37, Sheet 38, and other building level plans (37-41) using the vision tool and reviewed the symbol legends. While parking stall dimensions are clearly shown in the legends, no dimensions are shown for the vehicular drive aisle widths between rows of parking spaces or for internal driveway widths within the parking garage. The vision tool confirmed that 'there are no dimension lines or tick marks spanning across these driving areas' and 'no text labels within the plan view of the parking garage indicating drive aisle or circulation width'. Used semantic search to query 'parking aisle width drive aisle circulation width' across the entire plan set, which returned only results about parking stall dimensions and ADA access aisles, not vehicular circulation widths.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires parking aisle widths or internal driveway widths to be dimensioned. These dimensions are necessary for TPW to verify that the garage layout provides adequate maneuvering space and meets transportation design standards. While the parking space dimensions are shown, the drive aisle widths between parking rows are not dimensioned on any of the building level plans. The absence of these dimensions constitutes the deficiency described in CC-22-20.
findings.explanation: Parking stall dimensions shown, but drive aisle widths not dimensioned on any building level plans (Sheets 37-41)
findings.resolution: Add dimension lines on the parking garage floor plans showing the width of drive aisles between rows of parking spaces and internal driveway circulation widths.

findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 16 (Site Notes And Tables), specifically Block 1 containing the parking table. The table includes a detailed 'PARKING MIX' section with columns breaking down spaces by type. The breakdown shows: STANDARD PARKING PROVIDED - 500, COMPACT - 57, EV READY - 31, EV CAPABLE - 10, and ADA PARKING SPACES section showing VAN and STANDARD subcategories totaling 26 ADA spaces. Additionally, Sheet 37's symbol legend defines the space type codes (R, C, HC, VAN) used throughout the garage plans. Block 3 on Sheet 37 provides a 'RESIDENT PARKING PROVIDED PER LEVEL' table further breaking down parking by type across all garage levels.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires parking spaces to be identified by type (standard, compact, handicapped, bicycle). Sheet 16's parking table clearly identifies and quantifies all parking space types, with specific counts for each category. The building plans (Sheet 37) reinforce this with symbol legends and per-level breakdowns. Bicycle parking is also shown in the table with required and provided counts. This comprehensive identification satisfies the completeness requirement for TPW to verify parking type compliance with code requirements.
findings.explanation: Sheet 16 parking table identifies spaces by type: 500 standard, 57 compact, 26 ADA (handicapped), plus bicycle parking

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan 1 OF 2) using the vision tool. The sheet's legend (Block 5) defines a dotted line pattern (small open circles) as 'PROPOSED ADA PATH'. The vision analysis confirmed that this dotted line pattern is 'extensively visible throughout the site plan' with paths entering from Collier Street and Kinney Avenue, running along the southern 9' sidewalk, and branching to connect to the main building infrastructure. The vision tool confirmed 'a clear, continuous dotted line entering the site from the right-of-way on Collier Street...travels south into the site, crosses a drive aisle...and terminates directly at...PROPOSED BUILDING ENTRANCE'. The accessible route system connects public sidewalks to building entrances and the parking garage area.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires an accessible route of travel to be shown connecting all accessible elements. Sheet 14 uses the PROPOSED ADA PATH symbol (dotted line) to clearly delineate a connected accessible route network throughout the site. The vision analysis confirmed continuous paths from public ROW to building entrances and parking areas, with ramps at transition points. This graphic representation on the site plan satisfies the completeness requirement for demonstrating ADA/TAS-compliant connectivity.
findings.explanation: Sheet 14 shows continuous accessible routes (dotted ADA path lines) connecting public sidewalks, building entrances, and parking areas

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan 1 OF 2) using the vision tool. Block 3 on Sheet 14 contains 'KEY NOTES' which define callout marker <12> as 'PROPOSED ADA RAMP'. The vision analysis identified 'at least 6 distinct locations where the <12> callout is used to denote a proposed ADA ramp', including: near the northwest corner (Kinney Ave area), along the eastern side of the main northern entry drive from Collier Street, in the central area where paths cross drive aisles, and at the southern edge along the 9' sidewalk. These ramp callouts are placed 'where the dotted ADA paths cross drive aisles or transition at curbs'.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires ramps connecting accessible elements to be shown on plans. Sheet 14 uses the <12> callout marker to identify proposed ADA ramps at multiple locations where the accessible route encounters grade changes, curbs, or drive aisle crossings. The vision analysis confirmed at least 6 ramp locations are called out, demonstrating that ramps are explicitly shown and located on the site plan. This satisfies the completeness requirement for identifying accessibility ramp locations for TPW and building review.
findings.explanation: Sheet 14 shows at least 6 ADA ramps marked with callout <12> at curb transitions and accessible route crossings

findings.observation: Reviewed the parking table on Sheet 16, which shows 647 total private parking spaces provided on-site (in the building's parking garage across levels 1-5) and 23 Collier public parallel parking spaces on the public street. Conducted a grep search across the entire project directory for terms 'off-site parking', 'off site parking', and 'offsite parking' with case-insensitive matching. The search returned no matches. Reviewed the Consolidated Site Plan Application document and found no mention of off-site parking arrangements. The parking is entirely provided on the subject property within the building structure.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item OSP-01 has a condition: 'If proposing off-site parking'. Based on the comprehensive review of the site plan documents, the project proposes all parking on-site within the building's parking garage. No off-site parking (parking on a separate parcel to meet the subject property's parking requirements per LDC § 25-6-501) is proposed. Since the condition for applicability is not met, this checklist item does not apply to this site plan submission.
findings.explanation: No off-site parking proposed; all 647 parking spaces provided on-site in building garage

findings.observation: Reviewed the parking table on Sheet 16 and the site plans. All parking is provided on-site in the building's parking garage (647 spaces across levels 1-5). Conducted a grep search for 'off-site parking' terms across the project, which returned no matches. No off-site parking arrangements are documented in the Consolidated Site Plan Application or other supplementary documents. The 23 Collier public parallel parking spaces noted in the parking table are public street parking, not off-site parking controlled by the applicant to meet parking requirements.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item OSP-02 has a condition: 'If proposing off-site parking'. This item requires walking distance dimensions to be shown when a project uses off-site parking to meet LDC § 25-6-501 parking requirements. Since no off-site parking is proposed for this project (all parking is on-site in the building), the condition for applicability is not met. findings.explanation: No off-site parking proposed; all parking on-site, so walking distance dimensions not applicable

summary: 8 of 14 items pass, 4 items fail, 2 items not-applicable. Failures: driveway spacing dimensions (CC-22-12), curb return radii (CC-22-13), opposing driveway offsets (CC-22-15), and parking aisle widths (CC-22-20).
